name: Modafinil
drug_class: Wakefulness-promoting agent (eugeroic); atypical dopamine reuptake inhibitor
route_note: Oral tablets once daily in the morning (or before a work shift for shift work disorder).

discovery.by: Laboratoire L. Lafon; clinical work by Michel Jouvet (Lyon)
discovery.note: Identified as the active metabolite of adrafinil, a Lafon compound found to promote wakefulness in animals in the 1970s.

tagline: Wake-promoting drug for narcolepsy, sleep apnoea and shift work sleepiness
summary: Modafinil is a wakefulness-promoting drug used for excessive sleepiness due to narcolepsy and, in the US, obstructive sleep apnoea and shift work disorder. Its main action is weak dopamine transporter inhibition; it is less euphoriant than amphetamines but still carries some misuse potential and is widely used off-label as a 'smart drug'.
mechanism: Modafinil binds the dopamine transporter and inhibits dopamine reuptake, increasing extracellular dopamine, which is required for its wake-promoting effect in animal studies. It also increases histamine, noradrenaline, serotonin, glutamate and orexin activity and reduces GABA in arousal-related brain regions, probably downstream of dopamine.
Unlike amphetamine it does not cause transporter-mediated monoamine release, which may contribute to its lower abuse liability.
uses: Residual excessive sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnoea (US, adjunct to CPAP)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Lafon chemists identify modafinil as a metabolite of adrafinil.

history.title: French approval
history.detail: Modafinil is approved in France as Modiodal for narcolepsy.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Provigil (Cephalon) is approved for narcolepsy in December 1998.

history.title: New indications
history.detail: The FDA approves modafinil for obstructive sleep apnoea and shift work disorder.

history.title: Settlement
history.detail: Cephalon pays $425 million to settle allegations of off-label promotion of Provigil and other drugs.

history.title: EU restriction
history.detail: The EMA restricts modafinil to narcolepsy because of skin, psychiatric and cardiovascular risks.

history.title: FTC settlement
history.detail: Teva pays $1.2 billion to settle FTC claims that Cephalon delayed generic Provigil through pay-for-delay deals.

pk.metabolism: Hepatic amide hydrolysis and CYP3A4; induces CYP3A4 and inhibits CYP2C19

facts: Modafinil induces CYP3A4 and can make hormonal contraceptives less effective during and for a month after use.
